item.title: Target makes the case for how it will ‘reclaim its merchandising authority’ at annual investor day
item.description: During an investor meeting that Target hosted at its Minneapolis headquarters on Tuesday, senior leaders spelled out the company's plans to reclaim its merchandising authority in key areas including food and beauty.

item.title: Vitamin Shoppe debuts ‘Suppie Awards’ and SuppCo unveils certification program as third-party validation drives category growth, plus news
item.description: This week, I checked in with Muriel Gonzalez, president of The Vitamin Shoppe, and Steve Martocci, founder and CEO of supplement tracking app SuppCo. The former debuted its inaugural "Suppie Awards" last week through a sponsored partnership with Hearst Magazines, while SuppCo unveiled a new "Tested by SuppCo" certification program on Tuesday with a who’s who of supplement brand participants.

item.title: Bath & Body Works is leaning on content creators, reworking packaging and formulations to recoup sales
item.description: As part of its Consumer First Formula turnaround plan announced in November, the Ohio-based personal care company is implementing new strategies to reinvigorate consumers in a competitive market. That includes modernizing its packaging and formulations to keep up with new demands.

item.title: Evereden co-founder and CEO Kimberley Ho on giving equity to Gen Alpha
item.description: As influencer marketing evolves beyond one-off paid posts, brands are finding new ways to build relationships that last, and go deeper than a hashtag-sponsored post.

item.title: Fashion Briefing: As war engulfs the Middle East, fashion brands are already feeling impacts on stores and foot traffic
item.description: While the political and humanitarian impacts of large-scale war in the Middle East are still playing out, the region's fashion and luxury market is already affected. Over the last few years, countries like Qatar and the UAE have positioned themselves as glamorous luxury destinations, courting heritage European brands and wealthy consumers from around the world. Now, many of those brands are closing stores and relocating employees away from danger.

item.title: Sephora doubles down on K-Beauty hair care
item.description: This year, Sephora does not plan to slow its investment in K-Beauty. On April 1, the retailer will launch its second K-beauty hair-care brand, LG-owned Dr. Groot, online. That will be followed by an in-store rollout on April 15.

item.title: Luxury Briefing: As cashmere spreads downmarket, luxury brands update their approach
item.description: For this week’s Luxury Briefing, I spoke to the CEO and creative director of Agnona Stefano Aimone about the brand’s new flagship store and material innovations. Also, insights on the relaunch of Robert Marc, a buyer's take on Dior and news to know.

item.title: A buyer’s take on Milan Fashion Week, with Bloomingdale’s Marissa Galante Frank
item.description: On this week’s Milan Fashion Week edition of the Glossy Podcast, senior fashion reporter Zofia Zwieglinska is joined by Marissa Galante Frank, fashion director at Bloomingdale's, for a buyer’s perspective on the Fall 2026 collections.

item.title: How brands are showing up around the LA Marathon this weekend
item.description: Glossy checked in with brand leaders at Asics, Hoka, Strava, Therabody, Lululemon and more to learn about the planned activations, including official sponsorships and proximity-based events, in Los Angeles ahead of this weekend’s big race.

item.title: Glossy Pop Newsletter: Inside the new era of long-wear makeup
item.description: Long-lasting makeup — able to withstand face masks, meetings, dinners and dates — is increasingly top of mind for everyday consumers; it's no longer solely the concern of celebrities being photographed on the red carpet.
